questions.question: Describe the rule for 3; 7; 11; 15 and give the eighth term.
questions.expected_answer: The differences are all 4, so the rule is add 4. Continuing: 19, 23, 27, 31 — the eighth term is 31.

questions.question: Why is 2; 6; 18; 54 not a constant-difference pattern, and what is its rule?
questions.expected_answer: The differences 4, 12, 36 are not equal. Each term is three times the previous one, so the rule is multiply by 3; the next term is 162.

questions.question: Explain from the diagram why each new matchstick square in a row adds 3 sticks, and give the number of sticks in shape 10.
questions.expected_answer: Each new square shares one side with the previous square, so only three new sticks are needed. Starting from 4 and adding 3 nine times gives 31.
